name: Turkey Stew with Carrot, Celery, Parsley & Peas over Rice
ingredients: 16 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a medium saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel, trim, and small dice carrots; trim and small dice celery. Place both in a medium bowl.
Peel, halve, and small dice onion; peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl with the carrot and celery.
Preheat a large pot over medium-high heat.

Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add turkey, veggies, and spices; cook, breaking the turkey apart with a spoon, until the veggies are softened and turkey is browned and crumbly, 4-5 minutes. (Reserve bowl for later use.)
Meanwhile, shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
When the turkey is done, add tomatoes, broth, peas, and soy sauce to the pot; stir to combine and bring the stew to a boil.
Meanwhile, in the reserved bowl, make a slurry by whisking water with cornstarch until smooth.
Once the stew is boiling, reduce heat to medium, and add the slurry in a steady stream while stirring. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until thickened, 2 minutes more.
Add half of the parsley to the stew, stir to combine, and remove from heat. (Reserve remaining parsley for serving.)
To serve, divide rice and stew between bowls; sprinkle with reserved parsley and enjoy!
author: Mealime
